scenarios.name: rag-ingest-with-cosine-and-citations
scenarios.rationale: Both use PersistentClient, get_or_create_collection, upsert, the cosine configuration, source/page metadata, and [0]-indexed query results passed to the LLM, but A adds a stable id with a content hash (slightly off the file-page-chunk spec), stale cleanup and a full prompt builder, while B follows the id spec exactly and is more compact, with a thinner LLM prompt step.

scenarios.name: filtered-search-price-range
scenarios.rationale: Both use query_texts, n_results=5, $and with $gte/$lte, and read ids[0] and distances[0]; A also says lower is closer and gives cosine similarity as 1 - distance, which the rubric asks for. B says lower is closer and names the default l2 metric but leaves out the cosine relationship.

scenarios.name: server-setup-and-migrate-hnsw-config
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric element: the server command, HttpClient with heartbeat, the configuration hnsw space form, space immutability, and the 1.0 auth removal with a reverse proxy or Chroma Cloud. B gets the server, client and configuration right, and it says the space is fixed, but it omits heartbeat and never states that built-in auth was removed in 1.0 (it only says auth options changed between versions). B also adds unrequested migration code.
